label: unrelated-or-unexplained-hunk
name: A file change, removed comment, qualifier sweep or build flag that no body sentence or source branch accounts for
description: What breaks: content enters main that nobody reviewed on purpose. stats/.gitkeep deleted in a one-file gof.cpp fix (3197414598 'was this intentional?'); a 'DO NOT RENAME as packaging is dependent' comment removed in a PR about something else (3973917755 'why did this comment get removed? It's still relevant'); `volatile` added to 19 dma_qcsr_t members in a merge PR though neither main nor hwattention_sync has it (2629374536 'So where is this coming from?'); -mavx/-mfma flags added to the pos library with no explanation of why it built before (2670498736). Procedure (check 10 plus three triggers it currently excludes): also fire on deleted or added files absent from the body and commit subjects, on removed comment lines whose text names an external consumer (packaging, parsed by, DO NOT RENAME), on merge or sync PRs for content absent from both parents, and on added build flags (ask which symbol failed without them).
disposition_reason: Check 10 fires on hunks with no PR identifier in a feature PR; the corpus adds file deletions, removed consumer-protecting comments, merge-PR content absent from both parents and build flags.
agent_feasibility: yes: file-list vs body diff, removed-comment keyword scan, diff against both parents; the build-flag provenance needs a build.

members.concern: Asks whether the deletion of stats/.gitkeep (an empty placeholder file that keeps the stats/ directory in git) was intended, since the PR is described as a one-file fix in src/tron/gof.cpp.

detection.trigger: the diff deletes, adds or renames a file that no body sentence and no commit subject mentions, especially a zero-byte placeholder (.gitkeep), a stats/log file, or a file outside the directories the title names
detection.procedure: list files in the PR diff with `gh pr diff N --name-only` (or git diff --name-status BASE..HEAD); for each file, grep the PR body and commit subjects for its path or directory; for deletions, check `git show BASE:<path>` exists and whether any PR commit message explains the removal
detection.question: does the PR body or any commit subject account for this file change, or is it a by-product of the author's working tree (debug run, editor, stale stash)?

members.note: Verified in the worktree: stats/.gitkeep was deleted by commit 0da7929d7d ('Additional debug, and one posisble bugfix') and restored by 70bfbc833e ('restore stats/.gitkeep') after the comment. The author replied 'no, it was not. and I'm not sure HOW it happened.' Wade approved at eb0627f006 in the same minute, before the restore. Skill check 10 as written would not fire: a deleted empty file has no removed non-blank line, and the procedure keys on hunks, not on file-level add/delete.

members.concern: A diff hunk deletes the comment above min_bitfile_major/minor that says 'DO NOT RENAME as packaging is dependent on finding these values'; Wade asks why it was removed, says it is still relevant, and asks for the typo 'copatible' to be fixed while it is there.

detection.trigger: A hunk in a file the PR touches for another reason removes comment lines (or constants) that exist at BASE and whose text names an external consumer ('DO NOT RENAME', 'packaging', 'parsed by', 'depends on'), while the PR body and commit subjects say nothing about that removal.
detection.procedure: For every removed comment block in the diff: grep BASE for the identifiers the comment protects (here `min_bitfile_major`, `min_bitfile_minor`) outside h/ and src/; CMakeLists.txt:820-835 at main regex-parses `min_bitfile_<part> = <n>;` out of h/pos/config.hpp to build the deb package dependency string, so the comment's claim is true. Check whether the commit that removed it is a merge of main or a feature commit (`git log -S'DO NOT RENAME' -- h/pos/config.hpp`), and whether the body or any commit subject describes the removal. If nothing does, ask why.
detection.question: Does this removed line protect something still true at BASE (a consumer outside the file), and does any sentence in the PR explain removing it?

members.quote: why did this comment get removed? It's still relevant AFAIK (and `copatible` should get updated to `compatible`)
members.note: The comment at main h/pos/config.hpp:103-105 sits above `inline constexpr uint8_t min_bitfile_major = 5; ... min_bitfile_minor = 8;`. The top-level CMakeLists.txt:820-835 on main regex-extracts `min_bitfile_${BITFILE_VERSION_PART}` from that header and fails configure with 'Cannot read min_bitfile_...' if absent, then builds the package dependency string (archer-ia860m-*-standard >= version). So the comment's warning has a real consumer. The hunk (h/pos/config.hpp +2 -10 in a 23-file tracing PR) removed it with no body or commit mention; chander-positron replied the removal was accidental, restored it and said he would re-scan the diff for similar collateral deletions. Relation to check 10: the check is about unrelated hunks whose revert keeps the body true; the trigger would fire (removed lines exist verbatim at BASE, no PR identifier in added lines) but the procedure bins comment-only removals as 'do not fire', so as written it would miss this. A worthwhile extension: comment-only removals that name an external consumer are candidates.

members.concern: Wade asks where the new `volatile` qualifier on every member of dma_qcsr_t (the DMA queue control/status register struct) comes from, since neither main nor the hwattention_sync branch (the two sources of this merge PR) has it.

detection.trigger: A hunk in a merge or sync PR changes existing lines (here: adds a qualifier to 19 struct members) and the PR body does not mention that change.
detection.procedure: For each hunk whose removed lines exist at BASE, grep the added form in every branch the PR body names as a source (`git grep -n '<added text>' origin/main -- <file>`, same for the other source branch). If the added lines exist in none of them, the hunk is new content hidden inside a merge step. Also read the comment above the struct: here it says the struct 'should be declared as volatile' at the mapping site, which is a different place than the member qualifiers.
detection.question: Does this added content exist on any branch the PR claims to merge from, or in a body sentence; if neither, where did it come from and should it be here?

members.quote: I'm a bit confused by this... I don't see where these are 'volatile' in either latest main, or in latest hwattention_sync. So where is this coming from?
members.note: Read: at commit 2d7f3a62ec every member of dma_qcsr_t carries `volatile` (common.hpp lines 84-103) and dma_qcsr_debug_dump takes `const volatile dma_qcsr_t*`. `git log -S'volatile uint32_t ctrl' -- h/pos/dma/common.hpp` shows the qualifiers entered in 89a89f9a5b (the PR's first commit) and left in 1545a47a7a 'Removed interim change.' (22 insertions, 27 deletions; 19 removed '-  volatile' lines). The final PR diff keeps only the debug-dump helpers and uses memcpy from the volatile pointer. Check 10 fit is partial: its procedure keys on a 'What changes' identifier set and SIDE/MAIN bins; this PR body is one sentence and the hunk changes a qualifier, not a renamed identifier. The new element is comparing against the merge source branches.

members.concern: Wade asks whether the newly added -mavx/-mfma/-mavx2 and AVX512 compile options on the `pos` library target are what was missing to build, and puzzles over why his own builds of the test code compiled without them (a transitive include supplying the flags).

detection.trigger: A diff adds compiler feature flags or compile definitions (target_compile_options, target_compile_definitions, -m* flags) to a library target that previously built without them.
detection.procedure: Read the CMake hunk; grep CMakeLists.txt files for the same flags on other targets (e.g. `git grep -n 'mavx512' -- '*CMakeLists.txt'`) and for `target_link_libraries(... pos ...)` to find whether a dependent target already carried them PUBLIC; check which translation units in src/pos now include AVX intrinsics (grep `immintrin.h`, `_mm512`).
detection.question: Why did this target build before without these flags, and does the change make the dependency explicit or duplicate flags already inherited?

members.quote: so this is what was missing from the pos library to get a build? The test code must be been getting these by way of a transitive include or something then, since I never had any problem compiling there. Hmph.
members.note: Wade relies on his own build experience of the test code on this branch ('I never had any problem compiling there'); an agent could answer the provenance question by reading CMake targets but not his personal build history. No change requested; approved 1 minute later.

codex_bullets.bullet: Trace each changed area to the stated behavior or an explicitly requested bundled change. Suggest splitting unrelated cleanup. A missing body sentence alone does not make a necessary regression test unrelated.
codex_bullets.reason: Five comments (PRs 4557, 1920, 2148, 2659, 3016). Claude check 10 has the full procedure; the third sentence matches check 10's "regression guard" clause.
